t.5.52.1: Then the monkey, gazing upon Laṅkā, his heart's desire fulfilled and his zeal ever growing, reflected on what remained of his task.
t.5.52.2: What, indeed, now remains for me to do here at this moment that would cause these rākṣasas still greater torment?
t.5.52.3: The grove has already been ravaged, the foremost rākṣasas have been slain, and a portion of the army has been destroyed; what remains is the destruction of the fortress.
t.5.52.5: This fire, the bearer of oblations, that blazes on my tail, it is fitting to satisfy with these splendid mansions.
t.5.52.4: Once the fortress is destroyed, the task would require only easy toil; with little effort in this undertaking, my labour would bear fruit.
t.5.52.6: Then the great monkey, his tail ablaze, like a rain-cloud with lightning, roamed over the rooftops of the mansions of Laṅkā.
t.5.52.7: Hanumān released a fire that resembled the flames of the fire of universal destruction.
t.5.52.8: And through its union with the wind, the fire, exceedingly swift and of great might, blazed up like the fire of universal destruction and grew ever greater.
t.5.52.9: The wind spread the blazing fire through those houses.
t.5.52.10: Those great mansions, studded with gems, with their latticework of gold and made of pearls and jewels, crumbled and fell apart.
t.5.52.11: Those mansions, their towers shattered, fell to the surface of the earth, like the dwellings of the Siddhas falling from the sky when their merit is exhausted.
t.5.52.12: He saw many-colored minerals, mingled with diamonds, coral, lapis lazuli, pearls and silver, flowing out from the mansion.
t.5.52.13: Just as fire is never sated with logs and grass, so Hanūmān is not in the least sated with slaying the lords of the Rākṣasas.
t.5.52.14: Enveloped in the flames of fire, with her foremost heroes slain and her warriors put to flight, that Laṅkā, overwhelmed by the force of Hanumān's wrath, became like a city struck down by a curse.
t.5.52.16: Having slain those very many rākṣasas, having shattered that grove of many trees, and having set fire to the dwellings of the rākṣasas, the great-souled one went in his mind to Rāma.
t.5.52.15: The great-minded Hanumān beheld Laṅkā in turmoil, its rākṣasas terrified and despondent, marked everywhere by fire with brightly blazing flames, like the earth struck down by the wrath of Svayambhū.
t.5.52.17: Having set the whole of Laṅkā ablaze, the great monkey, best among monkeys, then extinguished the fire on his tail in the ocean.
